how to keep your brain young
for the rest of your life

keep learning new skills

learn a new skill every year: an instrument, a language, a craft. the struggle of being a beginner is exactly what keeps the brain building new pathways as you age.

move every single day

walk, swim or dance for at least thirty minutes a day. what's good for your heart is good for your brain, because both depend on the same healthy flow of blood.

stay social

keep seeing friends and making new ones, even when it takes effort. real conversation is one of the hardest workouts your brain does, and loneliness ages it faster.

a lesson a day

spend 5 minutes a day learning about something you know nothing about: astronomy, architecture, ancient history. a brain that keeps getting surprised keeps getting stronger.

protect your sleep

sleep seven to nine hours as often as you can. sleep is when the brain clears out the day and stores what matters, and nothing else can do that job for you.
